# TypeSafe Jev fixture provenance

The fixtures in this directory pin the **verified** TypeSafe System One wire
contract. They are copied from the official OpenAPI schema and documentation, so
the adapter is tested against the real field names, optionality and value shapes
instead of an invented format, so every field below is traceable to a source.

## Sources

| Source | URL | Captured | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Official OpenAPI schema, vendored into the official Python SDK as generated Pydantic models | `https://api.typesafe.ai/openapi.json` via <https://github.com/typesafe-ai/typesafe-sdk-python> → `src/typesafe_sdk/_schemas/models.py` (header: `generated by datamodel-codegen: filename: https://api.typesafe.ai/openapi.json`) | 2026-09-21 | `SystemOneRequest`, `SystemOneResponse`, `ChoiceQuestion`, `ChoiceAnswer`, `ValidationError`, `Usage` field names, types and descriptions |
| Official API reference — Choice primitive | <https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/choice> | 2026-09-21 | endpoint `POST /v1/systemone`; Choice returns `choice`, `probabilities`, `confidence`; a Choice question accepts up to 255 options; sum of probabilities is 1 |
| Official API reference — Score and Noul primitives | <https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/score>, <https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/noul> | 2026-09-21 | Score uses 2–10 ordered levels; Noul has no `confidence` field (checked because a missing confidence must fall back to the selected probability) |
| Official SDK transport | <https://github.com/typesafe-ai/typesafe-sdk-python> → `src/typesafe_sdk/_core/constants.py`, `_core/transport.py` | 2026-09-21 | authentication is `Authorization: Bearer <key>`; path constant `SYSTEM_ONE_PATH = "/v1/systemone"`; `Content-Type: application/json` |
| Official SDK configuration | <https://github.com/typesafe-ai/typesafe-sdk-python> → `src/typesafe_sdk/constants.py` | 2026-09-21 | default base URL `https://api.typesafe.ai`; default model alias `jev-latest` (accepted when explicitly configured) |
| Official SDK error handling | <https://github.com/typesafe-ai/typesafe-sdk-python> → `src/typesafe_sdk/_core/errors.py` | 2026-09-21 | status classification 400/401/403/404/422 vs 429 vs 5xx; validation error body shape `{"detail": [{"loc", "msg", "type"}]}` |
| Official site announcement | <https://typesafe.ai/blog/introducing-system-one-models-and-jev> | 2026-09-21 | product context only; no wire fields were taken from it |

The live `https://api.typesafe.ai/openapi.json` answered `503 no healthy
upstream` when fetched directly on 2026-09-21 (the API is in gated early
access). The schema used here is the copy the vendor's own SDK generation
publishes, which is authoritative for the wire format and is what the SDK and
its tests are built from.

## What each fixture covers

| File | Verified shape | Why it is kept |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `response_choice.json` | `SystemOneResponse`: `model`, `usage`, `answers.<id>` with a `choice` answer | the happy path: `choice`, full `probabilities`, `confidence` |
| `response_choice_no_confidence.json` | the same without `confidence` | Noul-style answers and any future shape without confidence must fall back to the selected candidate's probability |
| `response_choice_not_round_sum.json` | probabilities that sum to `0.9999996` | real JSON floats rarely sum to exactly 1; the tolerance must accept it and still normalize to exactly 1 |
| `response_choice_unknown_model.json` | `choice: "gpt-4o"` while the candidate set is different | the selected model must belong to the candidate set |
| `response_choice_missing_probability.json` | one candidate absent from `probabilities` | a partial distribution is a different question, not a weaker answer |
| `response_choice_extras.json` | unknown extra fields at the top level, in the answer and in `usage` | forward compatibility: unknown fields are ignored, not rejected |
| `response_validation_error.json` | `HTTPValidationError` with `detail[].loc/msg/type` | the documented 4xx body shape used by the error-summary tests |

Request fixtures are generated in tests from the golden bytes in
`request_choice.json`; they assert that the encoded request contains the pinned
model, every candidate's capabilities, the typed question and the conversation
verbatim — and, just as importantly, that no field the contract does not define
is sent.

## Deliberate divergences from the vendor's defaults

- The vendor SDK defaults a missing `model` to the alias `jev-latest`. This
  project leaves `jev.model` unset by default so the operator explicitly
  chooses a model identifier; upstream aliases are accepted and passed through
  unchanged when configured.
- The vendor SDK retries transport failures. This client performs **zero**
  retries for the same reason stage 3 does: a retried request can duplicate a
  billable evaluation.
- The vendor SDK validates answers with Pydantic and drops answer kinds it does
  not model. This client rejects the **whole** result when the routing answer is
  unusable, and never repairs a distribution by discarding entries.

To refresh these fixtures, re-read the OpenAPI schema in the official SDK
repository, update the JSON files, and record the new capture date and any
changed observations here.
